newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway gas group signs first deal with Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Norway gas group signs first deal with Ireland.

text.p: A consortium of gas producers has sealed the first contract to supply Norwegian natural gas to Ireland, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday.
The consortium comprising Statoil, Total Norge and Norsk Hydro ASA will sell 264 million cubic metres of gas to Bord Gais Eireann, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.

The gas will be piped from the North Sea Froey field through the Frigg line to St Fergus in Scotland. The sellers have an agreement with Statoil's British subsidiary, Alliance Gas, to pipe the gas to Britain's National Balancing Point.
Bord Gais Eireann has in turn contracted with British Gas Trading for the leg from the financial transaction point to Moffat in Scotland for onward transport through the UK-Irish interconnector line.
Statoil said the sales contract with Ireland covered about 75 percent of 1997 production from Froey. The remainder had been sold to Elf Petroleum under a separate agreement.
Licensees in Froey are Statoil with 53.96 percent, Total Norge with 15.23 percent, Norsk Hydro with 6.05 percent and operator Elf with 24.76 percent.
